figures.finding: The Children (Amendment) Act 2016, replacing section 8 of the Children Act, sets the minimum age of employment of a child at sixteen, and bars employing any child in work harmful or hazardous to the child, longer hours among them; the Employment Act 2006 (section 32), older, bars any employment under twelve and under fourteen allows only light work supervised by an adult over eighteen that does not affect schooling, and bars a child's work from 19:00 to 07:00. Layer 3 holds fourteen from the Employment Act; the later Children Act rule sets sixteen, and how the two are reconciled (whether light work from fourteen survives) is not stated in either text.

childrenAct2016.harmfulIncludes: working for longer hours, among others

value.conflict: later Act sets 16; reconciliation not stated

sources.said: For section 8 of the principal Act there is substituted the following— “8. Harmful Employment. (1) A person shall not employ or engage a child in any activity that may be harmful or hazardous to his or her health, or his or her physical, mental, spiritual, moral or social development. (2) Subject to subsection (1), the minimum age of employment of a child shall be 16 years.

(1) A child under the age of twelve years shall not be employed in any business, undertaking or work place. (2) A child under the age of fourteen years shall not be employed in any business, undertaking or workplace, except for light work carried out under supervision of an adult aged over eighteen years, and which does not affect the child’s education.

figures.finding: Uganda has no permit or licence for child performers: the general rules reach acting work as any other, so a child's employment is barred under sixteen by the Children Act (2016), and the Employment Act forbids a child's work from 19:00 to 07:00 and work a labour officer finds unsuitable; no hours-by-age, schooling or chaperone rule for performers exists, and nothing distinguishes writing or directing.

sources.said: (5) A child shal! not be employed between the hours of 7 p.m. and 7 am. … (4) A child shall not be employed in any employment or work which is injurious to his or her health, dangerous or hazardous or otherwise unsuitable

“harmful or hazardous employment” includes work which exposes a child to physical or psychological torture, sexual abuse, work underground, work at dangerous heights or in confined spaces, work with dangerous machinery, equipment and tools, or manual handling or transportation of heavy loads, work with chemicals and dangerous substances, work under extreme temperatures, high levels of noise, or working for longer hours;
